shouldFix.title: /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor was deleted, and with it the only record that Claude V8-A1 and V8-A2 remain open
detail: v9 carried the key /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor reading: 'CLAUDE-V6-A2 and CLAUDE-V6-A3 remain OPEN as namedOpenDecisions OD-2 on this surface (DR-103) ... V8-A1 and V8-A2 are carried: no further mutation of historical reMeasurementAtV2/V5 notes; no claim that adding reMeasurementAtV8 accounts for v7's unnamed reMeasurementAtV7.' v10 removes the key entirely. /appliesFindingsOf in v10 holds only claude2V9, codexV9, measuredAtAuthoring and standing.

I searched the whole v10 document for the strings 'V8-A1' and 'V8-A2'. Neither occurs anywhere. Neither was repaired - v10 folds only the four v9 findings - so two advisories that v9 explicitly recorded as OPEN and CARRIED now have no trace in the artifact. A reader of v10 cannot learn they exist.

The CLAUDE-V6-A2/A3 half of that record survives, because OD-2's decision text names them ('carried Claude v6 advisories V6-A2 and V6-A3') and OD-2 sits in /namedOpenDecisions. Only the v8 pair is lost, precisely because it had no home outside the deleted key.

The deletion is named only at parent granularity. META-v10's operation reads 'AMEND /basedOn and /appliesFindingsOf - predecessor is v9 52b3ab93...; Claude 2 v9 REJECT 0f15bd31...; Codex v9 REJECT 7eb3a857...' - it describes the verdict-record swap and says nothing about removing the carried-findings register. So basedOn.method's completeness claim survives at path granularity while a substantive removal goes undescribed. That is the same parent-named / child-change-undescribed pattern Codex identified in its v3 blocker B2.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: notFoldedThisSuccessor exists because this chain decided that findings which are carried rather than repaired must stay visible - it was introduced at v7 to answer exactly that question about CLAUDE-V6-A2/A3 and hardened at v8 and v9. Deleting it in the same revision that leaves two of its entries unrepaired removes the mechanism and its contents together. Every prior successor that carried a finding said so; v10 carries two and says nothing.
shouldFix.remedy: Restore /appliesFindingsOf/notFoldedThisSuccessor naming V8-A1 and V8-A2 as still carried, or record them wherever carried findings are now meant to live, and describe the change in a named operation rather than under the succession-bookkeeping entry.

shouldFix.title: Codex V9-A1 is neither folded nor recorded, and the repairLog's V9-A1 entry addresses the Claude finding of the same id with no collision declared
detail: The two v9 verdicts use the id V9-A1 for different findings. Mine is 'citationDiscipline is still written in v6's voice and is three successors stale'. Codex's is 'The V8-A3 repair entry imports a v1-verdict-citation defect that belongs to Codex V8-S1'. I read both verdict files to confirm this.

v10's repairLog contains one V9-A1 entry, whose verdictTitle is 'citationDiscipline is still written in v6's voice' and whose operation amends /sources/citationDiscipline. That is my finding, correctly repaired. Codex's V9-A1 is a different claim about a repairLog entry's attribution, and v10 neither folds it nor records it as carried.

v10's codexV9 record lists advisories ['V9-A1','V9-A2'] and carries a note - 'Codex V9-S1 is the same stranded corpus-v2 digest as Claude V9-S1' - which correctly declares the V9-S1 overlap but is silent on the V9-A1 collision. The effect is that Codex's advisory appears folded when it is not.

Every earlier round in this chain declared such collisions explicitly and disambiguated the ids: CLAUDE-V5-S1 and CLAUDE-V5-A1 at v6, CLAUDE-V6-A1 versus CODEX-V6-A1 at v7, V8-S1 versus CODEX-V8-S1 at v9 - the last of which v9 even spelled out inside basedOn.method. v10 drops that practice in the one round where it is needed.
Codex V9-A2 and my V9-A2 are the same finding (roster order), so no collision arises there and the single V9-A2 entry is correct.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: Carrying an advisory unfolded is legitimate; folding a differently-scoped finding under its id without saying so is not, because the repairLog is the audit record a later reviewer walks. Combined with V10-S1, the result is that three open findings - Claude V8-A1, Claude V8-A2, Codex V9-A1 - are invisible in v10.
shouldFix.remedy: Rename the entry CLAUDE-V9-A1, declare the collision in codexV9's note and in basedOn.method as v9 did for V8-S1, and either fold Codex V9-A1 or record it as carried alongside the V10-S1 restoration.

advisories.title: The 0444 freeze closes the digest cycle but permanently pins corpus v2 to a superseded predecessor, and v10 does not name that consequence
advisories.detail: The stranding I reported at v9 was caused by a mutual pin: corpus v2 pinned the schema, so adopting a new schema moved corpus v2's digest and broke the schema's citation of it. v10 breaks the cycle by freezing corpus v2 at 0444 and citing the frozen digest - a sound fix, and I verified both halves. The cost is that corpus v2 is now permanently pinned to schemas.v9 while its own reviewStatus is DRAFT-AWAITING-SCHEMA-SUCCESSOR. The successor has arrived - it is this subject - and the file can no longer adopt it without an unfreeze that would move the digest v10 cites. So the artifact now cites, as its live corpus-v2 reference, a draft that is frozen against the predecessor and cannot advance. Naming that - a corpus v3, or an unfreeze-and-recite protocol - would keep the next successor from rediscovering the cycle.
advisories.notBlocking: Every claim v10 makes about corpus v2 is true as measured, including 'draft against this schema lineage', since v9 is in the lineage.

advisories.title: The newly version-neutral citationDiscipline states a rule the sources block does not satisfy
advisories.detail: The repaired sentence reads 'Live pins at authoring N are recorded only at reMeasurementAtVN.' Read as universal it implies a reMeasurementAtVN for each authoring, but /sources holds only reMeasurementAtV2, AtV5, AtV6, AtV7, AtV8 and AtV10 - there is no AtV3, AtV4 or AtV9. The v9 gap is the one my V9-S1 named, and v10 correctly does not invent a v9 note for a frozen predecessor. The wording just needs to be conditional rather than universal - live pins, where a successor records them, are recorded at reMeasurementAtVN and nowhere else - which is the property the rule is actually for.
advisories.notBlocking: The rule's purpose, keeping live pins out of bindingSources and out of historical notes, is satisfied; only its quantifier overreaches.

advisories.title: OD-2's standing line still reads 'Not folded at v9' inside a v10 document
advisories.detail: v10 amends OD-2 to add registerEchoAtApplication but leaves standing as 'OPEN. Not folded at v9. Previously recorded at v8 /openDecisions[OD-V8-1]; moved here so this surface's open decisions are one lookup.' The sentence is historically true and the OPEN prefix carries the load, but a reader at v10 wants to know the decision is still not folded at v10. This is the same staleness pattern as the citationDiscipline finding I raised at v9, one field over, and the same one-word treatment closes it.
advisories.notBlocking: OD-2 is correctly recorded, findable in one lookup, and marked OPEN.
